name: Smart Forms by Livable Forms
author: tagglefish

sections.description:
Smart Forms by Livable Forms is a flexible WordPress form and lead-management plugin built for contractors and service businesses.

Create multiple forms, start from ready-made templates, publish each form with its shortcode, and manage every submission in WordPress. The plugin works without a paid license or required external service.

Forms and entries

  • Create and manage multiple forms
  • Drag-to-edit form builder
  • Per-form shortcodes
  • Starter templates for general quotes, roofing, HVAC, plumbing, painting, and electrical work
  • File and photo uploads
  • Searchable lead and entry dashboard
  • Lead detail views, notes, status, assignments, and activity history
  • Bulk entry and form management
  • Confirmation messages, redirects, and booking hand-offs
  • Responsive front-end forms

Notifications and workflow

  • Admin email notifications enabled by default
  • Optional customer auto-replies
  • Uses WordPress mail by default
  • Optional Resend delivery
  • Outbound webhooks
  • Optional Calendly booking links
  • Optional Google Calendar integration
  • Analytics, branding, and team controls
  • Honeypot, nonce validation, rate limiting, and optional reCAPTCHA

Smart Forms by Livable Forms stores forms and submissions in your WordPress database. You control your data and can keep using the plugin without connecting an outside account.

External services

Smart Forms by Livable Forms works without these services. They are contacted only when the site administrator configures or enables the related integration.

  • Resend — optional transactional email delivery. Form notification content and recipient addresses are sent to Resend when configured. Terms: https://resend.com/legal/terms-of-service Privacy: https://resend.com/legal/privacy-policy
  • Calendly — optional booking hand-off and event synchronization. Terms: https://calendly.com/terms Privacy: https://calendly.com/privacy
  • Google Calendar — optional calendar event creation using credentials supplied by the administrator. Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Google reCAPTCHA — optional spam protection when enabled. Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Webhook destinations — optional URLs selected by the administrator. Submission data is sent only to destinations the administrator configures.

Privacy

Smart Forms by Livable Forms stores submitted form data in the site’s WordPress database. Depending on fields created by the administrator, that data may include names, email addresses, phone numbers, project details, and uploaded files.

The plugin does not send submission data to Livable by default. Data is transmitted to an optional external service only when the site administrator configures that integration. Site owners are responsible for providing appropriate privacy notices and obtaining consent for the fields and services they enable.
sections.installation:
1. Install Smart Forms by Livable Forms from the WordPress Plugins screen, or upload the plugin ZIP.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Livable Forms in WordPress admin.
  4. Create a form or select a starter template.
  5. Copy the form shortcode and add it to a page, post, widget, or page-builder shortcode block.
  6. Review notification delivery under Livable Forms > Integrations.

New submissions appear in the Livable Forms entry dashboard.
sections.faq:
Is Smart Forms by Livable Forms free?

Yes. All included plugin features are available without a license key.

Does it require an external service?

No. Forms and entries work locally in WordPress. Email uses WordPress mail unless you optionally configure Resend. Calendly, Google Calendar, reCAPTCHA, and webhook destinations are optional.

Where are submissions stored?

Submissions are stored in your WordPress database and displayed in the Livable Forms entry dashboard.

Can I create more than one form?

Yes. Each form has its own fields, settings, status, entries, and shortcode.

Does it work with page builders?

Yes. Add the generated shortcode to Gutenberg or to a shortcode block in Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, and other page builders.

Can visitors upload files or photos?

Yes. File fields can be added to forms. Uploads are stored in the WordPress media/uploads environment and connected to the submission.

How are email notifications delivered?

The plugin sends through WordPress mail by default. You can optionally connect Resend. The Integrations screen reports missing configuration and delivery failures instead of silently treating them as successful.

Will deleting the plugin delete my forms and leads?

Not by default. Business data is retained unless the purge-on-uninstall option is explicitly enabled. Stored integration credentials and scheduled events are removed during uninstall.
sections.changelog:
2.22.4

  • Tested: confirmed compatibility with WordPress 7.1.
  • Changed: releases now use the native WordPress.org plugin update system.
  • Changed: updated the directory description, installation steps, FAQ, privacy disclosure, and external-service documentation to match the current multi-form product.
  • Confirmed: all included form-builder, notification, entry-management, webhook, booking, analytics, branding, and team features remain available without a license key.

2.22.3

  • Fixed: hardened database setup and upgrade handling for existing installations.
  • Fixed: kept historical form-entry metadata synchronized for entry sorting and reporting.

2.22.2

  • Added automatic update support for privately distributed builds. WordPress.org builds now use the native directory updater instead.

2.22.1

  • Corrected outdated internal product notes.

2.22.0

  • Restored the Integrations screen.
  • Added visible notification-delivery failure reporting and independent customer auto-reply handling.
